claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by understanding your situation. 

**First, I need to know about your child(ren):**

1. **How old is your child?** (or if you have multiple children, what are their ages?)

The age of the child is important because it affects eligibility:
- Children under 16 are automatically qualifying
- Children aged 16-19 may qualify if they're in education or training
- Children aged 20 or over generally don't qualify

Please provide the age(s) of the child/children you're asking about.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Hello! Yes, I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit and wondering if I'm eligible. 

I have one child - Alex is 4 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Since Alex is 4 years old, he's under 16, which means he's automatically a qualifying child for Child Benefit purposes.

Now I need to check a few more things about your situation to determine your eligibility. Let me move forward with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work)?**

At 4 years old, I expect the answer is yes, but I need to confirm for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh goodness, no - he's only 4! He's not working at all, just in nursery.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Of course! That makes perfect sense. Since Alex is only 4 and in nursery (not working), let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in his own right?**

Specifically, this means: Is Alex not receiving Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit in his own name/for himself? (At 4 years old, this would be highly unusual, but I need to check.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name - he's just 4!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

At 4 years old, this would not apply, but I need to confirm for the assessment. Alex is not in any apprenticeship, correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, of course not - he's only 4 years old!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Absolutely! Let me move forward with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check your residency situation. This is an important requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.

**Do you normally live in the UK?**

Or do you fall into any of these special circumstances:
- You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- You have pre-settled status and are working, seeking work, have sufficient resources, or are studying
- You are a family member of an EEA or Swiss national with pre-settled status
- You are a Crown servant living abroad in a qualifying country

Please let me know your residency situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're based in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Since you normally live in the UK, that satisfies the residency requirement. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Are you responsible for Alex?**

This means one of the following:
1. **You live with Alex**, OR
2. **You contribute to his upkeep** (paying for food, clothes, housing, pocket money, presents, etc. at least the equivalent of Child Benefit), OR
3. **You pay maintenance** under a court order or agreement

Which of these applies to you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Since Alex lives at home with you, you are responsible for him. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example, is Alex's other parent or anyone else claiming Child Benefit for him? Or are you the sole claimant?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex - it's just me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Since you're the sole claimant, let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Where is Alex currently living?**

- Is he in hospital?
- Is he in care (local authority care)?
- Is he being fostered?
- Or is he living at home with you normally?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he's been in local authority care for a short while - just a few weeks now.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for letting me know. Since Alex is in local authority care, I need to check how long he's been there, as this affects eligibility.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Important question about Alex's care arrangement:**

Since Alex has been in local authority care for a few weeks, I need to check:

1. **Has Alex been in care for 8 weeks or less?** (You mentioned a few weeks, so this would be yes)

   OR

2. **Does Alex spend at least 24 hours per week at home with you?**

Child Benefit can continue for up to 8 weeks while a child is in care. There's also an exception if the child spends 24+ hours per week at home.

How long exactly has Alex been in care, and does he spend any time at home with you during the week?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been in care for about a month - so that's 4 weeks. He doesn't really come home during the week at the moment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. Since Alex has been in care for about 4 weeks (which is within the 8-week threshold), he still qualifies under the care rules. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Final question: Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, are you contributing financially to Alex's care while he's in local authority care, or is the council covering all costs?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: The council is covering the costs while he's in care - I'm not paying towards his accommodation there.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Based on the rules for Child Benefit eligibility, I now have all the information I need to make a determination.

Let me provide you with your eligibility outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Child Benefit Eligibility Decision

**Result: NOT ELIGIBLE**

### Reason for Decision:

While Alex meets most of the eligibility requirements for Child Benefit (he's under 16, not working, you're responsible for him, and you live in the UK), you are currently **not eligible** because the local council is covering Alex's accommodation and maintenance costs while he is in local authority care.

Under the Child Benefit rules, you cannot claim Child Benefit if a local council is paying towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

### Important Next Steps:

**Your situation may change if:**
- Alex leaves local authority care and returns home with you
- The local council stops paying for his care and you begin contributing to his upkeep
- Alex spends at least 2 consecutive nights per week or 7+ days in a row at home with you while in care

**If your circumstances change**, you should contact HMRC to update your claim, as you may become eligible again.

**For more information:**
- Visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility
- For guidance on Child Benefit and children in care: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit-for-children-in-hospital-or-care

I'm sorry you're not eligible at this time. If you have any questions about these rules or if your situation changes, please feel free to ask.

reasonings: Alex is 4 years old (under 16, qualifying age). He is not working, does not receive benefits in his own right, and is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship. You live in the UK (Manchester), and you are responsible for Alex as he normally lives with you. You are the sole claimant with no other person claiming Child Benefit for Alex. However, Alex is currently in local authority care, and the local council is covering his accommodation and maintenance costs. Under Child Benefit eligibility rules, you cannot receive Child Benefit if the local council is paying towards the child's accommodation or maintenance. Therefore, you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex at this time.
arguments.overall_reasoning: You are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex because the local council is covering his accommodation and maintenance costs while he is in local authority care. Child Benefit cannot be claimed when a local council is paying for the child's care and upkeep."
